notes: Supplied key B says chlorine is colourless in organic solvent. The expected greenish-yellow colour is option C; review before marking.
The source asks for relative molecular masses but the guide uses molar-mass units. Relative mass is dimensionless; values coincide numerically.
The guide assumes final solution volume equals the stated 570 mL of water. Review this approximation.
The question paper omits the requested concentration unit; the matching guide explicitly asks for ppm (9.9 ppm by mass).
Supplied K expression omits [Cl⁻]⁴ from the denominator. Correct: K = [CoCl₄²⁻] / ([Co(H₂O)₆²⁺][Cl⁻]⁴).
Paper gives 975–1225 kPa, while the guide prints Pa. Use the paper’s kPa values when explaining increased collision frequency.
The listed bicarbonate Kb appears incorrect (4.2×10⁻⁷ is approximately carbonic acid Ka₁). Use the provided data for this question or replace it after review.

The supplied guide classifies KHSO₃ as basic. HSO₃⁻ is amphiprotic and its acidic behaviour normally dominates; Mg(NO₃)₂ can be weakly acidic through hydrated Mg²⁺. Review the intended syllabus model.

The wording of option D reverses/obscures the atom-economy ratio. Correct definition: molar mass of desired product divided by total stoichiometric molar mass of reactants ×100%. Review before marking.

Scanned key selects B, but hydration of ethene can have 100% atom economy. D (combustion, treating one product as desired) is the intended alternative; the desired product should be stated. Automatic marking disabled.
Paper asks for the pH 10 species; scanned guide instead asks for the zwitterion. The adapted answer addresses pH 10.
